title: How to Email a PhD Supervisor: 7 Templates and Practical Tips
content:
A supervisor email should make it easy to understand your preparation and research interests. Explain the specific connection to the group's work, ask one clear question and attach only what the programme requests.

Should you email a PhD supervisor before applying?

Often yes, especially for self-proposed doctoral projects. But not every advertised studentship expects direct contact. Read the programme instructions first. An email is not an application and a positive reply is not an offer. Oxford’s guidance recommends concise, individually tailored messages that show informed interest in the academic’s work.

Before writing: a five-minute research check

  1. Read the professor’s university profile and the lab’s current projects.
  2. Read at least one relevant paper and note its specific question or method.
  3. Check whether applicants must contact a supervisor before the formal application.
  4. Prepare a short CV and a one-paragraph summary of your research interests.
  5. Use an informative subject line, and write to one academic at a time.

Seven PhD supervisor email templates

1. Enquiring about available PhD supervision

Subject: Prospective PhD applicant — [research topic] — [entry year]

Dear Professor [Surname],

I am [name], currently [degree or position] at [institution]. My work on [specific project] introduced me to [research question]. I read your [paper/project] and was particularly interested in [specific, accurate detail].

I am considering a PhD focused on [one-sentence idea]. Are you expecting to supervise new doctoral students in this area for [year]? I have attached my CV and would be happy to share a brief research outline.

Kind regards,
[Name]

Replace every bracketed field with genuine, verifiable information. Do not claim to have read a paper you have not read.

2. Responding to an advertised funded PhD

Subject: Question about [project title] studentship

Dear Dr [Surname],

I am preparing an application for the advertised [exact project title], reference [number]. My background includes [relevant evidence], particularly [method or project]. Your project’s focus on [specific topic] connects with [what you actually did].

Could you clarify [one specific question not already answered in the advert]? I plan to apply through the official portal before [deadline].

Best regards,
[Name]

Replace every bracketed field with genuine, verifiable information. Do not claim to have read a paper you have not read.

3. Proposing a research idea

Subject: Potential PhD project on [specific research question]

Dear Professor [Surname],

I am interested in investigating [clear problem] using [proposed approach]. I noticed that your group studies [accurate research theme], and your work on [publication] helped shape the question I want to explore.

My preparation includes [evidence]. Would a project in this direction fit your group’s current research priorities? I can send a two-page outline if useful.

Kind regards,
[Name]

Replace every bracketed field with genuine, verifiable information. Do not claim to have read a paper you have not read.

4. Requesting a short discussion

Subject: Request for brief conversation about PhD research fit

Dear Dr [Surname],

Thank you for your work on [topic]. I am exploring doctoral applications in [area] and have [relevant project or experience]. Your [specific paper or lab initiative] is particularly close to [specific question].

If you are considering new PhD students, would you be open to a brief conversation about potential research fit? I appreciate that your schedule may not allow this.

Best,
[Name]

Replace every bracketed field with genuine, verifiable information. Do not claim to have read a paper you have not read.

5. Following up respectfully

Subject: Follow-up: prospective PhD applicant in [area]

Dear Professor [Surname],

I am following up on my email of [date] about possible PhD supervision in [area]. I understand you may be busy. I remain interested in [brief reason] and would appreciate any indication of whether you are considering applications.

Thank you for your time.

Kind regards,
[Name]

Replace every bracketed field with genuine, verifiable information. Do not claim to have read a paper you have not read.

6. Asking about funding eligibility

Subject: Funding eligibility for [PhD project] — international applicant

Dear Dr [Surname],

I am interested in [project title] and would like to confirm one point before applying. I am an applicant from [country], and the advert mentions [exact funding description]. Does this award cover international tuition fees, or should I contact the doctoral admissions team about a fee shortfall?

Thank you for your guidance.

Best regards,
[Name]

Replace every bracketed field with genuine, verifiable information. Do not claim to have read a paper you have not read.

7. Replying to a supervisor who is not taking students

Subject: Thank you for your reply

Dear Professor [Surname],

Thank you for letting me know. I appreciate your time and understand that you are not accepting new doctoral students.

If you happen to know of a group working on [specific topic] that is recruiting, I would be grateful for a suggestion, but I understand if not.

Kind regards,
[Name]

Replace every bracketed field with genuine, verifiable information. Do not claim to have read a paper you have not read.

What to attach and what to avoid

  • Usually attach a short, relevant academic CV; add a proposal only if requested or helpful.
  • Use a professional email address and name PDFs clearly.
  • Do not send the same generic email to 50 professors.
  • Do not ask questions answered clearly on the project page.
  • One polite follow-up after roughly 7–14 days is reasonable; silence is not a judgement of your potential.
  • Do not treat agreement to discuss a project as guaranteed funding or admission.

Frequently asked questions

Can I email several potential supervisors?

Yes, when each professor is genuinely relevant. Personalise messages separately and be transparent if an institution asks about other applications.

Will a professor reply?

There is no guaranteed response rate. Workload, available places and funding affect replies; these templates cannot guarantee an answer.

Official guidance and further reading

  • Oxford: contacting a potential supervisor

An email should have one clear purpose

Before writing, decide whether you are asking about research fit, future recruitment or an advertised position. For a live vacancy, read the application instructions first. A message might say: “I am considering the advertised project on [topic]. In my dissertation I used [method] to investigate [problem]. I would like to ask whether experience in [specific area] would be relevant to the project.” This is an illustrative structure: use only details that are true. A focused question gives the recipient something concrete to answer without asking them to assess an entire application by email.

Relevant listings and guides on NextApply

To see how these questions apply to a real listing, review Citizen-Centred Artificial Intelligence CDT PhD 2027. Compare its stated requirements with your own preparation and check the official source before applying.

You can also browse Northumbria University on NextApply and the doctoral training programmes category. Listings and recruitment windows can change.
